claims.text: The method is applicable to high-entropy alloys containing five or more principal elements.
The applicable temperature range is approximately 1800–3500 K and includes both solid and liquid phases.
Relevant HEAs include equimolar Nb–Ti–Zr–Hf–(X) alloys and AlCoCrFeNi.
An EAM reference can be replaced by an ab initio-trained machine-learning potential such as a Moment Tensor Potential or Deep Potential.
An active-learning deep neural-network potential can be initialized from AIMD configurations of crystalline and liquid states at 3500 K and iteratively enriched through exploration and labeling.
Active learning can generate training sets tailored to the relevant system and configurational space rather than relying on a fixed training set.
The enhanced active-learning protocol will specifically capture rare, high-energy liquid configurations.
The proposed potential uses high-dimensional local-environment descriptors including neighbor distances, angles, and many-body correlations.
These descriptors allow one potential to capture both ordered solid structures and diverse disordered liquid configurations.
Training on a broad, actively selected ensemble of ab initio configurations more accurately reproduces the target system's many-body interactions.
The actively learned potential will improve reference–target phase-space overlap relative to an EAM reference.
Improved phase-space overlap will shorten the free-energy integration path.
The shorter or better-matched integration path will reduce cumulative thermodynamic-integration errors relative to conventional EAM-based methods.
The thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will decrease by approximately 40–50% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Traditional TOR-TILD using EAM reference potentials is the relevant baseline.
Insufficient coverage of configurational space can limit the accuracy of a machine-learning potential.
The predicted performance outside the stated composition and temperature ranges, or with insufficient ab initio training data, is uncertain.
The hypothesis is to be tested by comparing EAM-based TOR-TILD and actively learned deep-potential free-energy calculations for the same HEA near melting.
Failure to reduce integration error by at least 20%, or failure to reproduce important ab initio phase-space regions, is designated as falsifying the hypothesis.
